status: drafted single-pass by reading the full extracted Geneva 1560 verse text directly (all 22 chapters), cross-checked against the existing KJV Revelation.json for tier-naming-style precedent only - content/structure independently grounded in this translation's own text, not copied from KJV's file.
notes: Revelation in the Geneva 1560 translation tells the identical canonical narrative found in KJV - the same 22 chapters, the same seven letters to the churches, the same seven-seals/seven-trumpets/seven-vials escalation, the same antagonist trio (Dragon, Beast from the sea, False Prophet/Beast from the earth), the same fall of Babylon, marriage supper, thousand years, great white throne, and New Jerusalem close. No apocryphal or structural content differences were found (unlike, e.g., this project's already-confirmed Ethiopian Ezra case) - this is a genuine same-canon, same-book comparison, so the tier structure below closely parallels KJV's Revelation.json by design, not by unverified assumption. Real translation-level differences ARE present and are worth flagging, though none change the roster of managers/tiers: (1) archaic period spelling throughout ("Iesus"/"Iohn" for Jesus/John, "Hierusalem," "Arma-gedon" hyphenated, "Hallelu-iah" hyphenated, "Labe" once at 5:6 - almost certainly a typesetting/OCR artifact for "Lambe" given the surrounding verses consistently use "Lambe," flagged rather than silently corrected); (2) Geneva 19:16 reads "THE KINGS OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS" (plural "Kings") where KJV famously has the singular "KING OF KINGS" - a real, quotable wording variant; (3) a genuine verse-division difference at the chapter 12/13 boundary - Geneva keeps "And I stood on the sea sand" as the final verse of chapter 12 (12:18), while KJV folds the same clause into the opening of 13:1 ("And I stood upon the sand of the sea, and saw a beast rise up...") - a versification difference, not a content difference, logged in genealogyLists rather than treated as missing/extra text. Naming-collision flags carried over from the same real-world figures: "that woman Iezabel" of Thyatira (2:20, Geneva's own spelling) is not the historical Jezebel wife of Ahab; "Antipas" the martyr of Pergamus (2:13) is not Herod Antipas the tetrarch (no Geneva NT Gospel index is confirmed built yet to cross-reference against, so this is logged generically rather than against a specific sibling file). The seer is named only "Iohn" (1:1, 1:9) - traditional identification with the Apostle is not asserted as textual fact. The Two Witnesses (11:3-12) are kept as a single collective person-type manager tier, per this project's embodiment test (they act, are killed, lie exposed, and are bodily raised - not mere transmission), never differentiated as individuals by the text. The seven letters and the closing angelic-guide framing at 1:1/22:6 are law-type tiers attributed to Jesus Christ (direct speaker of the letters) and John (receiver/recorder of the visions) respectively via "deliveredBy." Two distinct angelic guide references are kept as separate submanagers under John rather than merged, since the text itself never equates them: the unqualified "his Angel" of 1:1/22:6, versus the angel explicitly and repeatedly titled "one of the seuen Angels, which had the seuen vials" at 17:1/19:9-10/21:9/22:8-9.

scribeTiers.scribeName: First and Last, Aliue for Euermore
The Booke Sealed with Seuen Seales
A Woman Clothed with the Sunne
The Beast Rising from the Sea

characters.name: Iohn (the Reuelator)

verses.note: 'The Reuelation of Iesus Christ, which God gaue vnto him... sent, and shewed by his Angel vnto his seruant Iohn, Who bare record of ye word of God, and of the testimonie of Iesus Christ, and of all things that he saw.'
'I Iohn, euen your brother, and companion in tribulation... was in the yle called Patmos, for the worde of God, and for the witnessing of Iesus Christ.'
'I was rauished in spirit on the Lordes day' and hears a trumpet-like voice commanding him to write in a book and send it to the seven churches of Asia.
On seeing the risen Christ, 'I fell at his feete as dead.'
Takes the little book from the Angel's hand and eats it - 'sweete as honie' in his mouth, bitter in his belly once eaten.
Falls before the angel's feet to worship him; is corrected: 'See thou doe it not... Worship God.'
'I Iohn sawe the holie citie newe Hierusalem come downe from God out of heauen, prepared as a bride trimmed for her husband.'
Falls down to worship the angel a second time and is corrected again.
John's closing warning against adding to or diminishing 'the wordes of the prophecie of this booke.'

funFacts: Falls down to worship the guiding angel twice (19:10 and 22:8-9) and is corrected both times, a repeated detail preserved identically in this translation.
Named only 'Iohn' throughout - the traditional identification with the Apostle John is not made explicit anywhere in this book's own text.

characters.name: Iesus Christ (Reuelation)
characters.scribeTier: First and Last, Aliue for Euermore

verses.note: 'that faithful witnes, and that first begotten of the dead, and that Prince of the Kings of the earth... made vs Kings and Priests vnto God euen his Father.'
Seen among seven golden candlesticks as 'one like vnto the Sonne of man' - white hair, eyes as flame of fire, feet like fine brass, a two-edged sword from his mouth.
'I am that first and that last... I am aliue for euermore, Amen: and I haue the keyes of hell and of death.'

Announced as 'that Lion which is of the tribe of Iuda, that roote of Dauid,' then seen 'in the middes of the throne' as a Lambe (rendered once as 'Labe' at 5:6, likely a typesetting artifact - see notes) 'as though he had bene killed,' who takes the sealed book.
Opens each of the seven seals in turn.
Cross-referenced from the harvest vision - 'one sitting like vnto the Sonne of man,' the same title used of him at 1:13, reaps the earth with a sharp sickle.

Rider on the white horse, 'Faithfull and true,' clothed in a blood-dipped garment named 'THE WORD OF GOD,' with 'THE KINGS OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS' (Geneva's plural rendering, vs. KJV's singular 'KING of kings') written on his garment and thigh.
In the New Jerusalem, 'the Lord God almightie and the Lambe are the Temple of it... the Lambe is the light of it.'

'I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end, the first and the last'; 'I am the root and the generation of Dauid, and the bright morning starre'; 'Surely, I come quickly. Amen. Euen so, come Lord Iesus.'

funFacts: Given his own Geneva-Revelation-specific manager id, distinct from any Gospel portrayal, per this project's established per-book Jesus rule.
Geneva 19:16 reads 'THE KINGS OF KINGS' (plural), a genuine wording variant from KJV's more familiar singular 'KING OF KINGS.'

characters.name: The Letter to Ephesus
characters.purpose: Commends the church's labour and patience and its testing of false apostles, but rebukes it for having 'left thy first loue,' calling it to repent and 'doe the first workes' or have its candlestick removed.

verses.note: Commended for works, labour, patience, and finding false 'Apostles' to be liars.
'Thou hast left thy first loue... repent, and doe the first workes: or els I will come against thee shortly, and will remooue thy candlesticke.'
Commended for hating 'the workes of the Nicolaitanes, which I also hate.'
Promise: to eat 'of the tree of life which is in the middes of the Paradise of God.'

characters.name: The Letter to the Smyrnians
characters.purpose: Addressed to a church suffering real poverty and coming tribulation, with no rebuke at all - only a call to remain 'faithfull vnto the death' for the crowne of life and freedom from 'the second death.'

verses.note: 'I knowe thy workes and tribulation, and pouertie (but thou art riche)... the blasphemie of them, which say they are Iewes, and are not, but are the Synagogue of Satan.'
'The deuill shall cast some of you into prison... be thou faithfull vnto the death, and I will giue thee the crowne of life.'
'He that ouercommeth, shall not be hurt of the second death.'

characters.name: The Letter to Pergamus
characters.purpose: Commends the church for keeping Christ's Name 'euen where Satans throne is' and even after Antipas's martyrdom, but rebukes it for tolerating the doctrine of Balaam and the doctrine of the Nicolaitans.

verses.note: 'I knowe thy workes and where thou dwellest, euen where Satans throne is... euen in those dayes when Antipas my faithfull martyr was slaine among you.'

Rebuke for those who 'maintaine the doctrine of Balaam, which taught Balac to put a stumbling blocke before ye children of Israel, that they should eate of things sacrificed vnto Idoles, and commit fornication.'
Also rebuked for those who maintain 'the doctrine of the Nicolaitanes'; called to repent.
Promise: hidden manna, 'a white stone, and in the stone a newe name written, which no man knoweth sauing he that receiueth it.'

characters.name: The Letter to Thyatira
characters.purpose: Commends growing love, service, faith, and patience, but rebukes the church for suffering 'the woman Iezabel' to teach and deceive the servants into fornication and idol-meat, with severe judgment threatened against her and her followers unless she repents.

verses.note: Commended: 'thy loue, and seruice, and faith, and thy patience, and thy workes... more at the last, then at the first.'

Rebuke: 'thou sufferest the woman Iezabel, which calleth her selfe a prophetesse, to teache and to deceiue my seruants to make them commit fornication'; given space to repent, refused; her children threatened with death.
Those who 'haue not knowen the deepenes of Satan' are spared any further burden.
Promise to him that overcometh: power over nations and 'the morning starre.'

characters.name: The Letter to Sardis
characters.purpose: A rebuke to a church with a reputation for life that is spiritually dead ('a name that thou liuest, but thou art dead'), urging watchfulness, with a promise of white array and preserved names in the book of life for the few who have not defiled their garments.

verses.note: 'Thou hast a name that thou liuest, but thou art dead.'
'Be awake, and strengthen the things which remaine, that are readie to die... I will come on thee as a thiefe.'
'Thou hast a few names yet in Sardis, which haue not defiled their garments.'
Promise: 'clothed in white araye, and I will not put out his name out of the booke of life.'

characters.name: The Letter to Philadelphia
characters.purpose: Receives no rebuke - commended for keeping Christ's word with only 'a litle strength,' promised 'an open doore, and no man can shut it,' and deliverance 'from the houre of tentation, which will come vpon all the world.'

verses.note: 'Thou hast a litle strength and hast kept my worde, and hast not denied my Name... I haue set before thee an open doore, and no man can shut it.'
Those 'of the Synagogue of Satan, which call themselues Iewes, and are not' made to worship before the church's feet.
Promise to 'deliuer thee from the houre of tentation, which will come vpon all the world.'
Promise: made 'a pillar in the Temple of my God,' inscribed with God's Name, the new Hierusalem's, and Christ's own new Name.

characters.name: The Letter to the Laodiceans
characters.purpose: The sharpest rebuke of the seven - 'luke warme' Laodicea is warned Christ will 'spewe thee out of my mouth,' called wretched, miserable, poore, blinde, and naked despite thinking itself rich; counselled to buy true riches, with the image of Christ standing at the door and knocking.

verses.note: 'Thou art neither colde nor hote... because thou art luke warme... I shall spewe thee out of my mouth.'
'Thou saiest, I am rich... and knowest not howe thou art wretched and miserable, and poore, and blinde, and naked.'
Counselled to buy 'gold tried by the fire,' white raiment, and eye salue.
'As many as I loue, I rebuke and chasten'; 'Behold, I stand at the doore, and knocke... I wil come in vnto him, and will suppe with him.'
Promise: 'to sit with me in my throne, euen as I ouercame.'

characters.name: The Throne Room and the Sealed Booke
characters.scribeTier: The Booke Sealed with Seuen Seales
characters.purpose: Shows the heauenly throne - God enthroned, four beasts, four and twentie Elders, and a booke sealed with seuen seales that none is found worthy to open until the slain-yet-standing Lambe takes it, establishing the vision of worship that opens the seals sequence.

verses.note: A throne set in heaven, one sitting 'like vnto a iasper stone, and a sardine,' a rainbow round about 'in sight like to an emeraude.'
'Foure and twentie Elders sitting, clothed in white raiment, and had on their heads crownes of golde.'
Four beasts full of eyes cry 'Holy, holy, holy Lord God almighty, Which Was, and Which Is, and Which Is to come.'
'Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receiue glory and honour, and power: for thou hast created all things.'
A booke sealed with seven seales; John weeps 'because no man was foud worthy to open, and to reade the Booke.'
'A Labe as though he had bene killed' (the text's own Lambe, likely a typesetting variant - see notes) takes the booke from him that sat on the throne.
All creation sings 'Worthie is the Lambe that was killed to receiue power, and riches, and wisdome.'

characters.name: The Seuen Seales
characters.purpose: Six of the seven seales are opened in sequence, releasing the four horsemen, the cry of martyred souls under the altar, and cosmic upheaval, building toward the seventh seal's silence.

verses.note: First seal: 'a white horse, and hee that sate on him, had a bowe, and a crowne was giuen vnto him... going forth conquering that he might ouercome.'
Second seal: a red horse; power given 'to take peace from the earth... there was giuen vnto him a great sword.'
Third seal: a black horse, balances in hand; 'A measure of wheate for a penie, and three measures of barly for a peny.'
Fourth seal: 'a pale horse, and his name that sate on him was Death, and Hell folowed after him... power ouer the fourth part of the earth.'
Fifth seal: souls under the altar cry 'How long, Lord... doest not thou iudge and auenge our blood.'
Sixth seal: great earthquake, 'the sunne was as blacke as sackecloth,' 'the moone was like blood,' stars fall, mountains and isles moved.
Seventh seal: 'silence in heauen about halfe an houre.'

characters.name: The 144,000 and the Great Multitude
characters.purpose: An interlude before the seventh seal's silence: 144,000 servants of God sealed, twelve thousand from each of twelve tribes, followed by an uncountable multitude from every nation, clothed in white with palms, who 'came out of great tribulation.'

verses.note: An angel seals 'the seruants of our God in their foreheads' - 'an hundreth and foure and fourtie thousand.'
Listed by tribe (Iuda, Ruben, Gad, Aser, Nephthali, Manasses, Simeon, Leui, Issachar, Zabulon, Ioseph, Beniamin) - Dan is not named, and both Ioseph and Manasses appear (see genealogyLists).
'A great multitude, which no man coulde number, of all nations and kindreds... clothed with long white robes, and palmes in their hands.'
'These are they, which came out of great tribulation, and haue washed their long robes, and haue made their long robes white in the blood of the Lambe.'
'God shall wipe away all teares from their eyes.'

characters.name: The Seuen Trumpets
characters.purpose: Seven angels sound seven trumpets, each releasing an escalating plague on earth, sea, rivers, and sky through demonic locusts and a vast army, building toward the seventh trumpet's declaration that the kingdoms of this world have become the Lord's.

verses.note: First trumpet: 'haile and fire, mingled with blood... the thirde part of trees was burnt, and all greene grasse was burnt.'
Second trumpet: 'a great mountaine, burning with fire, was cast into the sea, and the thirde part of the sea became blood.'
Third trumpet: a star called 'wormewood' falls, embittering a third of the waters.
Fourth trumpet: a third of sun, moon, and stars darkened.
Fifth trumpet: the bottomless pit opens, releasing locusts ruled by a king 'whose name in Hebrewe is Abaddon, and in Greeke he is named Apollyon.'
Sixth trumpet: four angels loosed at the river Euphrates lead 'twentie thousand times ten thousand' horsemen who kill a third of men.
Seventh trumpet: 'The kingdomes of this worlde are our Lordes, and his Christes, and he shall reigne for euermore.'
The Temple of God opened in heaven; the Arke of his couenant is seen.

characters.name: The Two Witnesses

verses.note: 'My two witnesses' prophesy 1,260 days in sackcloth - 'two oliue trees, and two candlestickes, standing before the God of the earth.'
Fire from their mouth devours enemies; power to shut heaven, turn waters to blood, and smite the earth 'with all maner plagues.'
'The beast that commeth out of the bottomlesse pit, shall make warre against them, and shall ouercome them, and kill them.'
Their corpses lie unburied 'in the streetes of the great citie, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt' for three days and a half.
'The spirit of life comming from God' enters them; they stand up and 'ascend vp to heauen in a cloude,' seen by their enemies.

funFacts: Kept as a full person-type manager tier rather than a law tier, matching the KJV file's own adversarially-corrected precedent: they act, suffer, are killed, lie exposed, and are bodily resurrected in full public view.
Never individually named or differentiated by the text - kept as one collective entry.
Popular tradition links them to Moses and Elijah; the text itself does not name them (see genealogyLists).

characters.name: The Woman and the Dragon
characters.scribeTier: A Woman Clothed with the Sunne
characters.purpose: A sign-vision of a woman clothed with the sun, in travail, opposed by a great red dragon waiting to devour her child; once the child (who is to 'rule all nations with a rod of yron') is caught up to God's throne, the dragon is cast to earth and pursues the woman, who is protected in the wilderness.

verses.note: 'A woman clothed with the sunne, and the moone was vnder her feete, and vpon her head a crowne of twelue starres... traueiling in birth.'
'A great red dragon hauing seuen heads, and ten hornes, and seuen crownes,' whose tail draws a third of the stars and casts them down, waiting to devour her child.
'Shee brought foorth a man childe, which should rule all nations with a rod of yron... her childe was taken vp vnto God and to his throne.'
The woman flees into the wilderness, fed 'a thousande, two hundreth and three score dayes.'
The dragon persecutes the woman; she is given 'two wings of a great eagle' and nourished 'for a time, and times, and halfe a time.'
The dragon casts a flood from his mouth after her; the earth swallows it up.
The dragon 'went and made warre with the remnant of her seede'; the chapter closes with John standing 'on the sea sand' - a real Geneva-specific versification break (see notes).
'The great dragon, that olde serpent, called the deuil and Satan, was cast out, which deceiueth all the world' - the text itself links this figure to the serpent.
War in heaven: Michael and his Angels fight the dragon; the dragon and his angels do not prevail, 'neither was their place found any more in heauen.'
Gives the beast 'his power, and his throne, and great authoritie'; men worship the dragon.
Unclean spirits 'like frogs' come out of the mouth of the dragon, beast, and false prophet.
An angel binds him 'a thousand yeeres' and casts him into the bottomless pit, sealed so he 'should deceiue the people no more' till the thousand years end.
Loosed for a season, he 'goe out to deceiue the people... euen Gog and Magog, to gather them together to battell.'
Fire from God devours the gathered nations; the devil is 'cast into a lake of fire and brimstone... tormented euen day and night for euermore.'

characters.name: Michael the Archangel

verses.note: 'Michael and his Angels fought against the dragon, and the dragon fought and his angels.'

funFacts: The only named angel who takes direct combat action against the dragon — he opposes and defeats the dragon in the war in heaven (Revelation 12:7-8), he does not serve or support him. Kept as a standalone character, not a submanager of Satan's tier, since the submanager pattern implies household/support for its parent manager and Michael is Satan's adversary, not his ally.

characters.name: The Beast from the Sea
characters.scribeTier: The Beast Rising from the Sea

verses.note: Rises 'out of the sea, hauing seuen heads, and ten hornes'; like a Leopard, feet like a bear, mouth like a lion; the dragon gives him 'his power and his throne, and great authoritie.'
One head 'wounded to death, but his deadly wound was healed, and all the world wondred and folowed the beast.'
Given a mouth speaking blasphemies and power 'to doe two and fourtie moneths.'
Given power 'to make warre with the Saints, and to ouercome them' over every kindred, tongue, and nation.
Worshipped by all whose names are not written in the Lambe's book of life.
Further described as 'was, and is not, and yet is'; the seven heads explained as 'seuen mountaines' and 'seuen Kings.'
Captured with the false prophet, both 'aliue cast into a lake of fire, burning with brimstone.'

characters.name: The False Prophet

verses.note: A second beast rises 'out of the earth,' having 'two hornes like the Lambe,' but 'he spake like the dragon.'
Exercises the first beast's power, causes the earth to worship it, does 'great wonders,' makes fire come down from heaven.
Deceives the earth into making 'the image of the beast'; gives it a spirit to speak and orders those refusing to worship it killed.
Causes all, small and great, to receive 'a marke in their right hand or in their foreheads,' without which none may buy or sell; number given as 'sixe hundreth threescore and sixe.'
Named among the unclean spirits gathering kings to battle.
'That false prophet that wrought miracles before him' captured with the beast and cast alive into the lake of fire.
Already in the lake of fire and brimstone when the devil is cast in, 'tormented day and night for euermore.'

funFacts: First introduced only as 'another beast' rising from the earth (13:11); only at 16:13 does the text give him the title 'false prophet.'
The number 666 (13:18) is presented as an instruction to count and identify the beast by number - the text does not itself state who this refers to.

characters.name: The Euerlasting Gospel and the Haruest
characters.purpose: Three angelic proclamations (the everlasting gospel, Babylon's foretold fall, and a warning against the beast's mark) followed by two harvest visions - grain and grapes - symbolizing final ingathering and judgment.

verses.note: The 144,000 stand with the Lambe on mount Sion, singing 'a newe song' only they can learn.
First angel proclaims 'an euerlasting Gospel'; 'Feare God, and giue glory to him: for the houre of his iugdement is come.'
Second angel: 'Babylon that great citie is fallen, it is fallen.'
Third angel warns against worshipping the beast or receiving his mark.
One 'sitting like vnto the Sonne of man' reaps the earth's grain harvest with a sharp sickle - cross-referenced into Jesus Christ's own manager entry, given the shared title.

An angel gathers 'the clusters of the vineyard of the earth' into 'that great wine presse of the wrath of God,' trodden 'without the citie,' the blood reaching 'vnto the horse bridles, by the space of a thousand and sixe hundreth furlongs.'

characters.name: The Seuen Vials of Wrath
characters.purpose: Seven angels pour seven vials of God's wrath in rapid succession - sores, sea and rivers to blood, scorching heat, darkness, the Euphrates dried to prepare the kings' way, and a final catastrophic earthquake - ending with the declaration 'It is done.'

verses.note: 'Seuen Angels, hauing the seuen last plagues: for by them is fulfilled the wrath of God.'
First vial: 'a noysome, and a grieuous sore' on those bearing the beast's mark.
Second vial: the sea 'became as the blood of a dead man.'
Third vial: rivers and fountains 'became blood.'
Fourth vial: men 'boyled in great heate' from the sun.
Fifth vial: the beast's kingdom 'waxed darke,' men 'gnawed their tongues for sorowe.'
Sixth vial: Euphrates dried up 'that the way of the Kings of the East should be prepared.'
Unclean frog-like spirits gather kings 'into a place called in Hebrewe Arma-gedon.'
Seventh vial: 'It is done'; the greatest earthquake 'since men were vpon the earth'; hail 'like talents' falls upon men.

characters.name: Babylon the Great and Her Fall
characters.purpose: A vision of 'the great whore' - a woman named 'A mysterie, that great Babylon' - arrayed in purple and scarlet, drunk with the blood of saints, riding a scarlet beast; followed by her sudden fall and the lament of kings, merchants, and shipmasters who profited from her.

verses.note: 'The damnation of the great whore that sitteth vpon many waters,' shown by an angel 'of the seuen Angels, which had the seuen vials.'
Seen sitting on a scarlet beast, 'arayed in purple and skarlet,' holding a golden cup 'full of abominations.'
'A mysterie, that great Babylon, that mother of whoredomes, and abominations of the earth.'
'Drunken with the blood of Saintes, and with the blood of the Martyrs of IESVS.'
The ten horns and beast 'shall hate the whore, and shall make her desolate and naked... and burne her with fire.'
'It is fallen, it is fallen, Babylon that great citie, and is become the habitation of deuils.'
Kings, merchants, and shipmasters of the earth weep and lament over her destruction 'for in one houre is thy iudgement come.'
A mighty Angel casts a great millstone into the sea: 'With such violence shall that great citie Babylon be cast, and shalbe found no more.'

characters.name: The Marriage Supper and the Rider on the White Horse
characters.purpose: Heaven rejoices over Babylon's fall and announces the marriage of the Lambe, the Church figured as his bride 'arayed with pure fine linnen'; the vision then turns to the triumphant rider on a white horse who defeats the beast, the false prophet, and the gathered kings of the earth.

verses.note: 'Hallelu-iah, saluation, and glorie, and honour, and power be to the Lord our God... he hath condemned that great whore.'
'The marriage of that Lambe is come, and his wife hath made her selfe ready... arayed with pure fine linnen... the righteousnesse of Saintes.'
'Blessed are they which are called vnto the Lambes supper'; the guiding angel corrects John after he attempts to worship him.
Heauen opened, a white horse, rider 'Faithfull and true,' clothed in a garment dipped in blood, named 'THE WORD OF GOD.'
Heavenly hosts follow on white horses; 'THE KINGS OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS' written on his garment and thigh.
The beast and kings gather to battle him; beast and false prophet 'both were aliue cast into a lake of fire, burning with brimstone.'
The remnant 'slayne with the sword of him that sitteth vpon the horse.'

characters.name: The Thousand Yeeres and the Great White Throne
characters.purpose: Satan is bound a thousand years while the martyred faithful reign with Christ; released briefly to deceive the nations one final time before final defeat, closing with the dead of all ages judged before the great white throne 'according to their woorkes.'

verses.note: Souls beheaded for the witness of Jesus 'liued, and reigned with Christ a thousand yeere.'
'This is the first resurrection... on such the second death hath no power.'
Satan loosed, deceives 'Gog and Magog... whose number is, as the sand of the sea'; fire from God devours them.
'A great white throne, and one that sate on it, from whose face fled away both the earth and heauen.'
'The dead, both great and small stand before God... iudged of those thinges, which were written in the bookes, according to their woorkes.'
'The sea gaue vp her dead... death and hell deliuered vp the dead... death and hell were cast into the lake of fire: this is the second death.'
'Whosoeuer was not found written in the booke of life, was cast into the lake of fire.'

characters.name: The New Heauen, New Earth, and Newe Hierusalem
characters.purpose: The book's final and highest vision - a new heaven and new earth, God dwelling with men, no more death or sorrow, the holy city newe Hierusalem descending 'as a bride trimmed for her husband' and described in full architectural detail, closing with the river and tree of life and the book's own final warnings and blessing.

verses.note: 'A newe heauen, and a newe earth: for the first heauen, and the first earth were passed away, and there was no more sea.'
'The holie citie newe Hierusalem come downe from God out of heauen, prepared as a bride trimmed for her husband.'
'The Tabernacle of God is with men... God shall wipe away all teares from their eyes: and there shalbe no more death, neither sorow, neither crying.'
'It is done, I am Alpha and Omega... I wil giue to him that is a thirst, of the well of the water of life freely.'
The angel 'which had the seuen vials full of the seuen last plagues' carries John to see the city: twelve gates named for the twelve tribes, twelve foundations named for the twelve Apostles.
The city foursquare, measured 'twelue thousande furlongs' on each side.
Walls of jasper, the city of pure gold, foundations of twelve precious stones, twelve gates each a single pearl.
'I sawe no Temple therein: for the Lord God almightie and the Lambe are the Temple of it... the Lambe is the light of it.'
'A pure riuer of water of life'; 'the tree of life, which bare twelue maner of fruits... the leaues of the tree serued to heale the nations.'
'There shalbe no more curse... they shall reigne for euermore.'
'Beholde, I come shortly... I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end, the first and the last.'
'I Iesus haue sent mine Angell... I am the root and the generation of Dauid, and the bright morning starre.'
Warning against adding to or diminishing 'the wordes of the prophecie of this booke.'
'Surely, I come quickly. Amen. Euen so, come Lord Iesus. The grace of our Lord Iesus Christ be with you all, AMEN.'

funFacts: Built as this file's closing tier, mirroring the KJV precedent of Revelation as the canon's own capstone vision - the tree of life reappears here, absent from scripture since Genesis 3:24.

characters.name: The Nicolaitanes

verses.note: Ephesus commended: 'thou hatest the workes of the Nicolaitanes, which I also hate.'
Pergamus rebuked for tolerating 'them that maintaine the doctrine of the Nicolaitanes.'

funFacts: Named in two of the seven letters; the text mentions them alongside Balaam's doctrine without stating the two are identical.

characters.name: Balaam (referenced)

verses.note: Pergamus rebuked for those holding 'the doctrine of Balaam, which taught Balac to put a stumbling blocke before ye children of Israel.'

characters.perkNote: A backward reference to the OT figure of Numbers 22-25/31 - not a new character being introduced in this book.

characters.name: Iezebel of Thyatira

verses.note: 'That woman Iezabel, which calleth her selfe a prophetesse,' teaches and deceives the church's servants; her followers threatened with tribulation and death unless she repents.

characters.perkNote: NAMING COLLISION FLAG: not the same person as Jezebel wife of King Ahab (1-2 Kings), who lived roughly nine centuries earlier - this appears to be the text's own chosen label for a local false teacher, not a claim of literal identity. Geneva spells the name 'Iezabel.'

characters.name: Antipas

verses.note: 'Antipas my faithfull martyr was slaine among you, where Satan dwelleth.'

funFacts: The only individually named martyr in the whole book.
characters.perkNote: NAMING COLLISION FLAG: not the same person as Herod Antipas, the tetrarch of Galilee who executed John the Baptist - two unrelated men sharing a name, the text gives no indication of identity between them.

characters.name: Death and Hell

verses.note: The pale horse's rider: 'his name that sate on him was Death, and Hell folowed after him.'
'Death and hell deliuered vp the dead... death and hell were cast into the lake of fire.'

funFacts: Personified as a pair in both appearances, never separated into individual action - one collective entry rather than two figures.

characters.name: His Angel (the Prologue's Reuealing Angel)

verses.note: Christ's Revelation is 'sent, and shewed by his Angel vnto his seruant Iohn' - the book's opening framing device.
'The Lord God of the holy Prophets sent his Angell to shewe vnto his seruants the things which must shortly be done' - the closing benediction reuses the same unqualified phrasing as 1:1.

characters.perkNote: NAMING/IDENTITY FLAG: 1:1 and 22:6 both refer only to 'his Angel,' without the 'seuen vials' qualifier used elsewhere (17:1, 21:9). Kept separate from the seven-vials angel below since the text never explicitly equates them.

characters.name: One of the Seuen Angels with the Seuen Vials

verses.note: 'One of the seuen Angels, which had the seuen vials, and talked with me, saying vnto me, Come: I will shewe thee the damnation of the great whore.'
Continuing the same vision, instructs John to write and corrects him after he attempts to worship.
'One of the seuen Angels, which had the seuen vials full of the seuen last plagues, and talked with mee, saying, Come: I will shewe thee the bride, the Lambes wife.'
Continuing the vision begun at 21:9, John again attempts to worship the angel and is corrected a second time.

funFacts: Explicitly identified by the same descriptive title at both 17:1 and 21:9 - the real textual marker distinguishing this figure from the unspecified 'his Angel' of 1:1/22:6.
Guides John through the book's two great closing visions: the judgment of Babylon and the vision of the New Jerusalem.

genealogyLists.note: Bulk or deliberately-unresolved references, kept out of the character list above.

twelve_tribes_of_the_144000.note: Geneva lists Iuda, Ruben, Gad, Aser, Nephthali, Manasses, Simeon, Leui, Issachar, Zabulon, Ioseph, Beniamin - 12,000 sealed from each. Omits Dan and lists both Ioseph and Manasses without a separate Ephraim entry, identical to KJV's own real variation from a typical OT tribal roster.

gog_and_magog_geneva.note: Reuses the Gog/Magog imagery originally from Ezekiel 38-39, applied here to a final end-times gathering of the nations rather than repeating that earlier historical setting.

moses_and_elijah_speculation.note: Popular tradition links the Two Witnesses to Moses and Elijah (fire-from-mouth, rain-stopping, water-to-blood parallels) - the Geneva text itself never names the two witnesses, so this is logged as tradition, not textual identification.

versification_note_ch12_13_boundary.note: A real, observed verse-division difference between this translation and KJV: Geneva keeps 'And I stood on the sea sand' as the final verse of chapter 12 (12:18), while KJV folds the identical clause into the opening of chapter 13 (13:1, 'And I stood upon the sand of the sea, and saw a beast rise up out of the sea'). This is a versification/chapter-boundary difference only - the underlying content and sequence of events is identical.

kings_of_kings_wording_variant.note: Geneva renders the rider's title 'THE KINGS OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS' (plural 'Kings'), a genuine wording variant from KJV's familiar singular 'KING OF KINGS' - flagged as a real translation difference, not an error.

labe_typesetting_note.note: The extracted text reads 'a Labe as though he had bene killed' where every other occurrence in this same chapter and book consistently reads 'Lambe.' Flagged as a likely period-typesetting or extraction artifact rather than a meaningful textual variant, per this project's practice of flagging rather than silently correcting anomalies in the extracted source text.

jesus_earthly_genealogy.note: Jesus's human genealogy is not restated in Revelation, which gives him only titles ('roote of Dauid,' 'Lion of the tribe of Iuda') - not indexed here.
